# Poof

> Poof is software that runs the back office for a small business. It categorizes, reconciles, job-costs, and closes the books, and puts every write in front of a person before it reaches the ledger: each proposal waits on a card with the evidence it found, the close is a record with a checklist the books tick off themselves, and the reconciliation ties to one figure. One plan, every feature, $79/mo. The brand sentence: "The work disappears. The evidence doesn't."

Poof is built by Austin Semple, a former controller: three years in audit, then seven running the books for small service businesses. It is a product of Semple Labs LLC.

Poof is one product on one plan. $79/mo (or $790/yr), every feature included, 30-day free trial, no credit card. A shop owner, a bookkeeper, a controller, or a firm runs the same software; service shops additionally get the AI receptionist, the dispatch board, and the technician's field link, at the same price. Poof does not sell a done-for-you bookkeeping service.

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://www.poofai.com): A five-act interactive walkthrough (the vanish, the approvals inbox, the reconciliation that ties, the close as a record, every claim with its evidence), a plain definition of Poof, six FAQs
- [Poof for shops](https://www.poofai.com/trades): the product page for service shops — an interactive walkthrough from an after-hours call to the Per-Job P&L, the receptionist, the technician's field link, deposits and prepaid plans, and FAQs. Same $79 plan.
- [The close](https://www.poofai.com/close): month-end close as a record: 17 tasks with business-day due dates, 13 evidence-bound and ticked by the books themselves, a reconciliation that ties to one figure with outstanding items carried forward, a signature that locks the period and captures what the month took; closed within five business days or the next month is free
- [Autopilot with limits](https://www.poofai.com/autopilot): AI that posts categorizations on its own inside limits you set (not a new account, under a dollar ceiling, merchant history unanimous and at least N deep, confidence over your bar), off by default, with standing rules that carry a ceiling and a daily cap and pause themselves on the first correction; no ledger rule can send anything to a customer
- [Features](https://www.poofai.com/features): All 128 features across 13 categories
- [Pricing](https://www.poofai.com/pricing): $79/mo, one plan, every feature, FAQs
- [How It Works](https://www.poofai.com/how-it-works): Three-step setup and automation overview
- [Poof vs QuickBooks](https://www.poofai.com/poof-vs-quickbooks): Side-by-side feature comparison with QuickBooks
- [About](https://www.poofai.com/about): Founder story, mission, company timeline
- [Security](https://www.poofai.com/security): Bank-grade security, SOC 2 audit logging, encryption, 2FA, RBAC

## Key Features (128 total across 13 categories)

**Job Costing, Month-End Close & Payments (20):** Job costing & per-job profitability (tag transactions, bills, and invoices to jobs; see profit per job — the trades headline feature), AP cash planner, period close & locking with immutable trial-balance snapshot, AI close narrative (plain-English month-end summary), monthly financial package (one-click close package: P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, variance), books-integrity checks, proactive insights engine (margin dips, unusual spend, cash risks), accept online payments (ACH or card via Stripe, auto-reconciled), inbound email capture (forward receipts and bills; AI extracts and files them), per-job labor allocation (technician hours land on the jobs they were spent on), financing gross-up (dealer fees recognized as a cost of the job), peer benchmarks on the per-job P&L, period tie-out engine, accrual roll-forward subledger, document playbooks (per-sender handling learned from corrections), customer deposits released on completion (a down payment on an install is held as a liability, not revenue, and released to that job's revenue when the job is done — the release previews first, refuses a deposit that isn't categorized as a deposit, and warns if the job was also invoiced), and maintenance plans that earn as visits are performed (a prepaid plan sale is deferred and each performed visit earns its share automatically when the tech completes a maintenance visit; a repair call on a plan customer does not count; two open plans on one customer is left for the office to pick; cancellation is a recorded decision — refund or forfeit — never a silent write-off; a visit that was both released and invoiced is flagged at month-end close). Prepaid (annual) plans are what ships; do not describe monthly-billed plan revenue. The close is a record (each month's close is one object — who started it, where it stands: not started / in progress / ready / signed / reopened, derived from the books — and what it took: locking the period is the signature, and the close captures transactions reviewed, entries posted, decisions by a person and by a rule, corrections, and hours from start to signature, plus a price and tier per close), a checklist with due dates that ticks itself (a template per organization; the trades default is 17 tasks in business days after month end, signed on day 7; twelve are evidence-bound and complete when the books prove them, cannot be ticked by hand, and each open one says why in a sentence and links to the screen that fixes it; manual tasks are a person's tick with who and when; every close stamps its own copy), and the nudge (a task past its due date on an open close is an insight, a card in Approvals with one-tap mark-done for a manual task, and one message per close per day on the shop's channels — Telegram, SMS, Slack, email — after re-reading the books so it never nags about work already done). The tie-out step reads "run the checks again" when a transaction was reviewed or an entry posted after the last run.

**AI-Powered Automation (9):** AI transaction categorization (BRAID engine), Poof AI assistant, AI chart of accounts generation, automated daily bookkeeping, AI recurring charge detection, receipt and invoice scanning (OCR with HEIC support), smart transaction matching, AI-guided onboarding, AI budget and forecast generation.

**Invoicing & Payments (8):** Invoicing with PDF export and email delivery, estimates with one-click conversion to invoices, credit notes, payment tracking, products and services catalog, customer management, recurring invoices, automated invoice follow-ups.

**Expense & Bill Management (5):** Expense tracking, mileage tracking, bill management, vendor management, transaction matching.

**Banking & Reconciliation (8):** Bank connection via Plaid (12,000+ banks), bank statement import (CSV/PDF with AI vision parsing), reconciliation (multi-step wizard with auto-match, hand match and unmatch, completion report with export and email, history with reopen and delete; works on a phone), auto-reconciliation (opt-in weekly or monthly; signs a period only when the difference is under a penny, otherwise each uncertain match becomes an approval card; takes the period after the last one completed so a missed month is caught up), outstanding items carry forward (a check written in July that clears in August is on August's book side; a first reconciliation lists what was open before it, never the opening balance; cleared rows stay cleared when the entry's memo or date is later edited), one figure on the screen and in the record (unexplained difference = statement ending − books at period end + booked-not-on-statement − on-statement-not-booked; the screen reads it from the server, completion stores the same number, the close's bank-reconciliation check reads that), deposits, multi-account support.

**Accounting & Reporting (8):** Double-entry accounting, 13 financial reports (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, Trial Balance, General Ledger, Account Detail, AR/AP Aging, Customer Sales, Vendor Expenses, Sales by Product/Service, Expenses by Category, Budget vs Actual), report drill-down, shareable report URLs, scheduled report delivery, financial import, accrual/cash basis toggle, recurring journal entry templates.

**Budgeting & Forecasting (5):** Budget creation (manual or AI-generated), budget lifecycle management, variance dashboard, 12-month cash flow forecasting with confidence bands, budget alerts.

**Team & Security (9):** Team management with 5 roles, two-factor authentication, SOC 2 audit logs with PII masking, session management, GDPR/CCPA-compliant account deletion, email verification, RBAC with 26 granular permissions, bot-abuse gate on registration (Cloudflare Turnstile), AI privacy chokepoint — every model call is PII-redacted before it leaves the process, routed to its configured destination, and logged with destination, model, redaction count, and token usage.

**AI Receptionist & Dispatch (12):** AI phone receptionist (answers the shop's line, knows its name, hours, and service area, and books the job), deterministic safety triage (gas smell, carbon monoxide, smoke, sparking, or an active alarm trigger immediate emergency escalation and a scripted "leave the building, call 911" response; no-heat below 45°F and no-cool above 95°F are emergencies too — these are rules in code, not instructions to a language model), real-calendar booking (availability computed from technicians, weekly windows, and time off, minus existing appointments and a drive-time buffer; the database refuses overlapping bookings), rule-based human escalation, multi-channel notifications (SMS, email, push, Slack, Telegram, webhook), dispatch board with call log and technician management, receptionist settings, manual-or-automatic dispatch (two independent switches: whether the AI picks who goes, and whether the system texts them), a customer record created on the first call and matched on the last ten digits of the number, automatic technician dispatch texts carrying the field link (a dispatcher can re-send by hand at any time), even work distribution (when several techs are free for a slot the job goes to whoever has the fewest jobs that day, then that week), and unassigned-job escalation (an appointment approaching its start with no tech assigned raises the alarm; emergencies are always auto-assigned regardless of the shop's switches). Skills are a PREFERENCE, not a gate — a tagged tech is preferred and an untagged tech is next, so a shop that has tagged nobody is never told it has no availability. This group is operator-installed as part of Poof for shops — Poof staff provision the number and the voice agent; it is not self-serve. CUSTOMER-FACING outbound texts (booking confirmation, reminder, "your tech is on the way") are NOT built; only the technician is texted — do not blur those two. It does not take payment on the call, optimize routes, or clone voices, and there are no outbound sales calls.

**Field Service & Job Handoff (10):** Technician field link (the tech opens their job from a text — no account, no password, no app install; the link is signed, opens exactly one job, is revocable, and a reschedule invalidates it), arrival tracking (on-my-way/arrived/completed recorded when they happen), field report (what was wrong, what was done, what still needs doing), equipment on file (the units at that address are a list the tech taps to attach; an unlisted unit is typed once and stays on file for whoever attends next — make, model, and serial follow the unit, not the visit), jobsite photos opted in or out of the customer invoice individually (the supply-house receipt showing shop cost defaults to not printing), parts and labor logged in the field tagged as labor/part/fee by the tech (parts picked from the shop's own price list so the invoice line lands on the right sales account, with the part's cost coming from the catalogue rather than the tech's form), the invoice writes itself (tap Complete and a draft invoice exists in the office in the tech's own words), trade-format invoice (diagnosis, work performed, recommended follow-up, equipment, warranty, with opted-in photos), and a completed service call becomes a job — linked to the customer with the invoice tagged to it, so the work reaches the Per-Job P&L without anyone tagging anything, and office review before it reaches the customer (the dispatcher opens the field report, photos, parts and labor, sign-off, the draft invoice, and — on a maintenance visit — the plan visit it earned or a one-click way to record one, from the board; the tech's internal notes are marked as never reaching the customer, and nothing goes out until a person sends it). Part of Poof for shops. The tech page does NOT do GPS tracking, does NOT take payment on site, records a typed name and timestamp rather than a drawn signature, and needs a signal — there is no offline mode. It does not schedule or re-route.

**Productivity & Workflow (6):** Personalized dashboard with AI daily briefing, global search, notification center, transaction approval workflows, command bar (Cmd+K), AI chat folders with drag-and-drop organization.

**Poof AI Capabilities (19):** Business-context-aware chat, books health check and month-end close guidance, invoice/estimate/credit note creation via AI, record creation via natural language, record updates, budgeting and forecasting guidance, recurring charge analysis, chart of accounts setup, account search and creation, journal entry creation with account validation, recurring journal entry setup (depreciation, amortization, rent, insurance), financial report generation, bank statement PDF import via chat, guided onboarding walkthrough, file attachment handling, approval inside the conversation (ask Poof to invoice someone and the same approval card appears in the chat with the same evidence and buttons as the inbox), and visible working steps (“Looking up invoices — August 2026”, “Preparing an invoice — Smith Residential” arriving as each step runs; the steps say preparing, never created, because nothing has been written yet). Ask where things stand ("Is August ready to close?", "which bills are due this week?", "what do we owe Ferguson?", "how did July go?" — the close's status and checklist, transaction search, A/P aging, open bills, the 13-week cash plan, accrual schedules, and a month's summary answered from the books; the model narrates the numbers and never computes new ones), and book, move, or cancel a visit from the chat (open slots and the appointment list answer at once; the booking becomes a card, and approving it runs the same handler the phone line runs; no rule can ever approve a visit).

**Approvals & AI Autonomy (9):** The approvals inbox (every write an AI proposes, from any surface — the nightly categorization sweep, a request typed into Ask Poof, a detector that noticed a job losing money — stages as a card and waits; nothing reaches the books until a person approves it, and approving runs exactly what is on the card, the stored request rather than a fresh interpretation of it), the evidence rather than the assertion (each card shows what Poof looked up to justify itself — the customer it resolved and their email, the prior transactions for that merchant and whether they were categorized the same way, the amount, the account — gathered by code, never judged by the model; a card saying “no history for this merchant” is telling you why it is asking), partial approval of a batch (untick three rows of forty, approve the rest in one tap, and the unticked ones are still waiting tomorrow), reject with a reason (the reason is recorded, not discarded — it is the signal that stops a rule covering that kind of work), standing rules granted from a card someone already read (derived from the work in front of you — the merchant those rows share, the agreement in their history, a limit above the largest one — shown in plain sentences with how much of the card it covers and the owner's own 30-day record with that kind of change, not a blank form), a rule that stops itself (correct anything a rule is about — not only the rows it happened to touch — or reject the kind of work it covers, and it pauses, says which correction stopped it, and waits to be resumed or revoked; every rule lives on one page with what it has handled and who granted it, and revoking is instant), five queues in one inbox (an inbox playbook run, a reconciliation match the scheduled job was unsure of, a POS deposit that came in short, a bill the cash planner put on hold, and a late close task are all cards in the same Approvals inbox; the original pages still work and deciding there is the same decision), the page settles the card (a card from a pipeline, a detector, or the scheduled job waits thirty days — a chat draft waits one — and closes when the record is decided on its own page; a decision different from what the card proposed is recorded as a correction, like a Reject), and a playbook that graduates as a rule ("Approve all like this" on an inbox-run card pins a rule to that playbook, only while the file keeps its columns, under a ceiling from the run's total). The approvals inbox is on for everyone. AUTONOMY IS OFF UNTIL A PERSON GRANTS IT, one rule at a time — there is no default and no global “let the AI do it” switch. No ledger rule can ever send anything to a customer: invoices and credit notes are always a human's decision. The phone is a separate channel a shop opts into: the AI receptionist talks to callers and books jobs inside rules written in code, and nothing granted in the books can reach it. A rule that writes to the ledger MUST carry a dollar limit or it does not run; there is also a daily cap whose overflow goes to the inbox rather than being dropped, and a requirement that prior human decisions agreed. Rules cannot be created from a settings screen, only from work someone reviewed. Against QuickBooks: QBO has bank rules and they auto-post — a QBO rule that is wrong keeps being wrong until somebody notices; none of the ceiling, cap, agreement requirement, or self-pausing exists in a bank rule.

## Key Numbers & Claims

- 128 total features, all included in every plan (no tiers)
- Every AI write is staged for human approval before it reaches the books — “Nothing reaches your books without you seeing it first.” Autonomy is off until a person grants a rule, one rule at a time
- Customer deposits are held as a liability and released to the job's revenue on completion; prepaid maintenance plans are deferred and earn per completed visit — "A down payment isn't revenue until the job is done. A plan isn't revenue until the visit happens."
- 6 receptionist notification channels (SMS, email, push, Slack, Telegram, webhook)
- Technician field link requires no account and no app install
- The five-day close guarantee: books closed within five business days of month end, or the next month is free
- 12,000+ bank connections via Plaid
- 13 financial reports
- 30+ AI assistant tools (create, update, search, send, generate, import)
- 95% AI accuracy rate
- 5-minute setup time (self-serve)
- 90% reduction in manual data entry
- 5 team roles, 26 granular RBAC permissions
- 30-day free trial, no credit card required (self-serve)
- 12-month cash flow forecast horizon with confidence bands

## Pricing

- **Monthly:** $79/mo, all 128 features included, one plan, no tiers
- **Annual:** $790/year ($65.83/mo, save $158)
- The price does not change with the number of technicians, trucks, or organizations on the plan.
- Comparison anchor: the fair QuickBooks Online comparison is Plus at $140/mo — the tier carrying job costing, budgets, and full reporting — not Simple Start at $38/mo, which is single-user. QuickBooks pricing verified August 2026.
- **Free trial:** 30 days, no credit card required
- **Money-back guarantee:** 30 days
- Poof is software. There is no done-for-you bookkeeping service, no managed monthly fee, and no paid diagnostic audit.

## Founder

Austin Semple — CEO and Founder. Three years as an auditor, then seven as a controller, working with small service businesses before founding Poof in June 2025. In 2026, Poof focused its go-to-market on bookkeeping for trade contractors — the audience Austin knows best from his controller career.
